description: Mechanic-first diagnostic sequences that prioritize verification and next tests before component replacement.

initial_questions: When did the concern start and what repair, weather, fuel, or driving condition changed recently?
Does the symptom happen cold, hot, at idle, under load, while braking, while turning, or after sitting?
Are there warning lights, stored codes, leaks, smells, noises, recent jump starts, or aftermarket electrical accessories?
quick_checks: Scan all relevant modules and save freeze-frame data before clearing anything.
Inspect basic fluid level/condition, battery/charging state, wiring, connectors, grounds, leaks, and visible damage.
Verify the customer complaint under safe conditions instead of replacing the most common part first.
diagnostic_sequence: Confirm the complaint, stored and pending codes, freeze-frame data, warning lights, and exact operating conditions.
Perform a visual and basic safety inspection before disassembly: fluid levels, battery state, connectors, grounds, leaks, belt condition, and obvious damage.
Reproduce the symptom when safe and compare scan-tool data, measurements, and customer history with the actual failure.
Separate electrical command, power/ground, sensor feedback, and mechanical operation before replacing any major component.
Repair the lowest-cost proven fault first, clear codes, road test or operate under matching conditions, and verify the symptom is gone.
common_causes: Poor connection, low fluid, air leak, restricted flow, worn service part, sensor bias, actuator fault, or mechanical wear depending on the verified system.
Previous repair disturbance, corrosion, contamination, heat damage, or intermittent wiring movement.
Control-module or major assembly failure only after circuit, command, feedback, and mechanical checks support it.
commonly_misdiagnosed_as: The most visible component near the symptom
A complete assembly replacement before circuit, fluid, or mechanical verification
An unrelated code that set as a consequence of the root fault
stop_and_repair_conditions: Brake pedal sinks, severe pull, grinding, smoke, fuel leak, overheating, low oil pressure warning, or charging failure while driving.
High-voltage hybrid/EV warnings require qualified high-voltage service procedures, PPE, isolation, and manufacturer information.
Do not continue running an engine with severe overheating, low oil pressure, active fuel leakage, or a flashing check-engine light with catalyst-damaging misfire.
